16                THE PRESIDENT:   Senator Golden.

17                SENATOR GOLDEN:   Thank you, Madam 

18   President.  

19                I rise today to honor those who have 

20   led the effort to recognize World Lymphedema Day.  

21                We are also making history here 

22   today in this chamber.  The New York State 

23   Legislature will today become the first governing 

24   body in the United States and the world to honor 

25   and recognize World Lymphedema Day.  Originally 


                                                                669

 1   inspired by National Lymphedema Awareness Day, 

 2   this effort has grown into a worldwide movement.

 3                Millions of Americans are affected 

 4   by lymphedema and other lymphatic diseases.  This 

 5   disease is common in cancer survivors, with 

 6   approximately 35 percent suffering with 

 7   lymphedema as a result of diagnostic treatment 

 8   procedures.  Despite the high numbers of 

 9   sufferers, researchers into potential treatment 

10   and cures lags far behind other similar physical 

11   and emotionally debilitating diseases.

12                Lymphedema is a disease that results 

13   in swelling, usually of the arms and legs, 

14   leaving people in severe pain or discomfort, and 

15   sometimes leaving them physically impaired.  

16   Raising awareness of this underreported and often 

17   misdiagnosed condition is imperative, since the 

18   potential for infection is greatly increased if 

19   not treated.  

20                It is only right that we recognize 

21   the advocates who devoted so much of their time 

22   and efforts to this condition.  And at the top of 

23   this list is Bill Repicci, executive director of 

24   the National Lymphatic Education and Research 

25   Foundation.  Bill is a true champion of the 


                                                                670

 1   cause.  Thank you for all that you do.

 2                Today we also honor a brave young 

 3   man, 5-year-old Nicholas Hernandez of Riverhead, 

 4   New York, as a youth ambassador for his 

 5   extraordinary efforts to promote lymphedema 

 6   awareness and research.  Nicholas was born with a 

 7   primary lymphatic disease, and his parents, 

 8   Enabel and Christina, have been tireless 

 9   advocates for the cause through fundraising and 

10   developing a network of supporters.  And we also 

11   have last year's ambassador as well, 7-year-old 

12   Emma Detlefsen.  Welcome.

13                I commend all of the advocates for 

14   their tireless ongoing efforts to bring more 

15   attention to lymphedema and for lymphedema 

16   research.  

17                I also commend my colleagues for 

18   their support on this great movement.  This is an 

19   open resolution at the desk, and I would hope all 

20   of you would sign onto it.

21                Thank you, and God bless the 

22   advocates and those that are suffering with this 

23   disease.  Thank you.
